title: Beha'alotcha: we remember the fish (Numbers 11:4–6)
hook: the people crave Egypt's fish and cucumbers, forgetting the whip

segments.voice: Yesterday, Pesach Sheni, the second Passover, and your line, second chances exist. Did someone get one, maybe you? Day four hundred forty-three.

You run into an ex at a party, and for one dangerous second you only remember the good parts. The road trip. The inside joke. The way they made coffee. Somehow the months of feeling small have gone blurry. Or it's an old job you hated, and now you catch yourself saying, the people were great, though. Memory is a generous editor. It keeps the flavor and cuts the cost. The Israelites, a year out of slavery, eating manna in the desert, do exactly this, and the Torah quotes their grocery list.
screen: `ONLY THE GOOD PARTS.` → `MEMORY, THE GENEROUS EDITOR.` → `A GROCERY LIST FROM EGYPT.`

segments.voice: Numbers eleven. The camp starts to crave. First the mixed crowd that came out of Egypt with them, then everyone, weeping in their tent doorways. They say: "We remember the fish, which we were wont to eat in Egypt for nought; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlic". And now, they say, our throats are dry, and there's nothing but this manna. It's such a vivid list you can almost smell it. Leeks and onions and garlic. But look at two words: for nought. Free. The fish in Egypt were free? The ancient rabbis laughed at that. The Sifrei, and Rashi after it, ask: these were people who weren't even given straw for free to make their bricks. Who was handing them free fish? No, the rabbis say, here's what free really meant. Free of commandments. Free of responsibility. In Egypt, nobody asked anything of them except labor, and nobody expected them to choose. That's a kind of ease, and it's real. Freedom is heavier. And notice what the list leaves out completely. No whip. No quota of bricks. No baby boys thrown into the river. The craving doesn't lie about the cucumbers. It just forgets everything around them. The Torah doesn't mock them for missing food. Missing things is human. It just puts their own words on the record, so anyone reading later can hear what nostalgia does.
screen: `THE CAMP STARTS TO CRAVE.` · `FISH, MELONS, LEEKS, GARLIC.` · `FOR NOUGHT? FREE OF WHAT?` · `THE LIST LEAVES OUT THE WHIP.` · then, large: `EGYPT WASN'T FREE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: notice nostalgia for a bad place. Breathe, and let one old place come back to you: a job, a relationship, a city, a habit you quit. Notice the first memories that arrive. Probably the cucumbers. Then, gently, ask for the rest of the picture. What did it cost you to be there? What did you leave for a reason? You don't have to hate the place. Just hold the whole memory, flavor and cost together. The bell holds the time.
Beha'alotcha, the portion of the lamps, and of the night the people wept for Egypt's fish and forgot its whip.
Your line: Egypt wasn't free. Today, when you catch yourself missing something you left, finish the memory before you act on it. Day four hundred forty-three.

howItsDone: The people's craving for Egypt's food in Numbers 11 is read in Beha'alotcha each summer; Jewish teachers often use Rashi's reading of "for nought" to talk about how the memory of slavery can be softened into longing.

they asked how slaves denied free straw got free fish.

fork.setup: you're in the desert, eating manna. someone sighs: remember the free fish in Egypt? how do the rabbis answer that "free"?
options: Egypt really did feed its slaves well.
free meant free of commandments, not free of cost.
the fish were a gift from Pharaoh.
fork.reveal: the Sifrei and Rashi: they weren't even given straw for free. "for nought" means free of the commandments: an easy kind of unfreedom.

original.note: Hebrew: for nothing, free. the word the people use for Egypt's fish.

trapdoor: what you thought: the people simply got tired of manna.
what it means: they remembered Egypt's food and forgot Egypt's whip.
what a scholar hears: the Sifrei asks how slaves refused straw could get fish for free, and reads chinam as free of commandments.
